historical_references.reference: Smirchchakravartins were the rulers of the Malwa region during the Gupta Empire in the 5th and 6th centuries.
historical_references.context: The Smirchchakravartins were an important dynasty in the central Indian kingdom of Malwa during the later Gupta period. They are known to have ruled from the city of Ujjain and were significant patrons of Buddhism.

historical_references.reference: The Smara or Smiras were a group of Hindu non-Brahmin tribes in ancient India who were known for their devotion to the god Shiva.
historical_references.context: The Smara or Smiras were a group of non-Brahmin tribes in ancient India who were dedicated to the worship of the god Shiva. They are believed to have originated in the southern Deccan region and were influential in the religious and cultural life of the region from the pre-Mauryan period to the 12th century CE.
